name: yq
summary: A portable command-line processor that applies jq-like expressions across YAML and several additional document formats, with sequence and all-input evaluation modes.

features.name: Multi-format document boundary
features.description: The upstream README and command interface document YAML, JSON, XML, INI, properties, CSV, TSV, and other input/output formats, with format selection by file detection or explicit flags.
benefits: Applies one expression-oriented tool across heterogeneous configuration formats
Makes conversion between supported formats available at the CLI boundary
costs: Format-specific typing, ordering, comments, and encoding rules affect semantics
A common expression surface cannot expose every capability of every format

features.name: Sequence and all-input evaluation modes
features.description: The official command documentation distinguishes eval, which applies an expression to each document in sequence, from eval-all, which loads all documents from all files and evaluates once; the pinned command implementations construct separate evaluators for these modes.
benefits: Supports independent document transformations and cross-document operations
Makes whole-input aggregation an explicit invocation choice
costs: All-input evaluation can increase memory use with large document sets
The same expression may have different behavior under sequential and aggregate evaluation

features.name: Document-aware transformation pipeline
features.description: yq exposes expression files, input and output format controls, multi-document YAML support, split-expression output, and in-place updates, forming a pipeline from decoder through expression evaluator to encoder or file writer.
benefits: Provides scriptable transformations while retaining document-oriented output options
Allows updates to be routed to streams, split files, or an existing file
costs: Output fidelity depends on decoder and encoder behavior for each format
In-place and split output modes add filesystem and naming failure modes

mathematical_views.question: How does an expression map documents between input and output format representations?
assumptions: A document is modeled as a format-specific decoded tree or value
The evaluator is treated as a partial transformation that can fail on unsupported structure or syntax
The view abstracts comments, anchors, scalar styles, and format-specific round-tripping details

mathematical_views.question: When do sequential document evaluation and all-input evaluation produce different transformation domains?
assumptions: Sequential mode maps an expression independently over each decoded document
Aggregate mode supplies the complete collection of decoded documents to one evaluator
The model abstracts parser buffering and does not claim equivalence between modes

benefits: One CLI can bridge several structured document ecosystems
costs: Format diversity expands compatibility and fidelity testing

benefits: Users can select per-document streaming or cross-document context
costs: Evaluation mode becomes part of expression correctness and resource planning

benefits: Output routing supports both pipelines and file-oriented workflows
costs: Writer and filesystem modes add operational variation beyond expression semantics
